lines: The testament testamentar and Inventar [of] umquhile Archibald Glasgow
maltman Indweller In leith [who] deceissit in the moneth of ffebry [1662]
givine up be Agnes Watsone his relict spous tutrix testamentar
in name and behalf of Archibald George and Williame Glasgowes minoris bairnes
lawfull to the said umquhile defunct
[the three sons] he nominat his onlie executoris in his latterwill
[inventory of malt, bear, household plenishing, and clothing]
Debtis awand to the deid: Jon Greig in Northleith; Williame Couper in Leith; Jon Watsone [and names/sums partly unresolved]
Debtis awand be the deid: Robert Cunynghame maltman in Leith; Williame Patersone; Williame Glasgow weiber in Leith; James Nisbit apothecar [and sums partly unresolved]
[servants' wages:] Agnes [surname illegible] and Jonet Dick[sone?]
I Archibald Glasgow maltman and Indweller in Leith [latterwill]
Archibald George and Williame Glasgowes my lawfull sones my onlie executoris
[goods to the three sons equally]
my weilbelovit spous Agnes Watsone [as] intromissatrix and tutrix
for the weill and behoove of my said childrene by the advice and consent of
captane George Cocke burges in Edinburgh and Thomas Glasgow weaver in Edinburgh as oversiars
[Agnes to administer during the children's minority with the overseers' consent]
this testament [was] writtin be Thomas Glasgow weaver in Edinburgh
at Leith the [day numeral unresolved] day of Jan[uar] 1662
witnesses Walter Roddie Indweller in Edinburgh and Robert Stewart stabler in Leith
[subscriptions of Archibald Glasgow, Walter Roddie, and Robert Stewart]
Sir John Nisbet [commissary/confirmation formula]
Thomas Glasgow weaver in Edinburgh [caution procedure]
[following James Davidsone testament excluded]

plain_english: Archibald Glasgow was a maltman living in Leith and died in February 1662.
Agnes Watson is expressly his surviving spouse. She acts as testamentary tutor and estate administrator for their minor children.
Archibald, George, and William Glasgow are expressly called his lawful sons and are his sole executors and equal beneficiaries after debts.

Captain George Cock and Thomas Glasgow, weaver in Edinburgh, are overseers. Thomas also wrote the will and appears in the caution procedure, but no surviving clause calls him Archibald's brother or other relative.
William Glasgow, weaver in Leith, is a creditor. His shared surname does not establish kinship.
findings: Confirmed explicit family: wife/widow Agnes Watson; lawful sons Archibald, George, and William Glasgow.
Confirmed legal roles: the sons are sole executors; Agnes is tutor/intromissatrix during minority; George Cock and Thomas Glasgow are overseers.
Confirmed associates: Walter Roddie and Robert Stewart are witnesses; Sir John Nisbet acts in confirmation; Thomas Glasgow is writer and appears in caution procedure.

Confirmed account participants include John Greig, William Couper, John Watson, Robert Cunningham, William Paterson, William Glasgow the Leith weaver, and James Nisbet the apothecary; the account does not state that any is kin.
Probable servant name Jonet Dickson remains qualified; Agnes's servant surname remains unreadable.
The testament defines a Leith maltman. Association with Glasgow-3078 is useful but not proved by this document alone because the securely documented 1647 heir was a Leith shoemaker.
changes_from_previous: No wife-or-sons conclusion changed; the explicit household is reconfirmed after a complete page-by-page name audit.
The reread inventories overseers, witnesses, officials, account parties, and servants separately and excludes unsupported kinship for both Thomas Glasgow and creditor William Glasgow.
The profile association is now expressly qualified at the occupation seam: maltman in 1662 versus shoemaker in the independent 1639/1647 chain.
unresolved: Exact January day on which the will was made

profiles: Maintained candidate association; do not treat the 1662 maltman identity as proved without bridging the occupation difference

Moderate for some account names and low for servant surnames and complete financial detail. The profile identity remains qualified.
